title: Belhomme
summary: Rehabilitation and rooftop extension of a corner building in Paris 18th, documented from a full survey of the existing facades.

quote.text: A project does not belong to its brief | it belongs to its site. Sometimes, you have to wait until the site is ready.

role.text: Production of all graphic documents from two separate digital models | existing and proposed | linked within a single reference file, ensuring consistency across demolition plans, regulatory sections, and facade elevations of the planning permission submission.

Originating from the Titi Barbès competition won by Studio BELEM in 2021 | residential and commercial rehabilitation and rooftop extension, boulevard Rochechouart, Paris 18th arrondissement. Project halted following a land ownership dispute, which delayed the permit submission for four years.

tag: Studio BELEM / From the Titi Barbès competition (2021) / Resumed under a new client | SNC HEMACLE / Ongoing

narrative.text: A corner residential building in Paris, its particular condition at the intersection of two streets creating a geometry that generates both problems and opportunities: obtuse room angles, a chamfered corner that reads as a landmark on the block, and party wall situations on two sides that require careful structural dialogue with adjacent buildings.

The rehabilitation addresses the envelope, the common areas, and the redistribution of the upper-floor apartments. The chamfered corner is treated as the compositional centre of the facade renovation, reinforcing its urban role. The project was conducted within the ABF regulatory framework, requiring close coordination with the heritage authority throughout the design and permitting stages.
